ios.desc:
One idea a day, from 12 fields that rarely share a room. Read it, carry it or let it go, then close the app. It takes two minutes. It stays with you much longer.

This morning it might be a Japanese word for sunlight through leaves. Tomorrow, why asking for help makes people trust you more. The day after, a quiet argument that doubt and conviction are not opposites. Philosophy, psychology, mathematics, language, history and the strange science of being a person. Put enough ideas in, from enough different places, and they start connecting on their own.

one card, one choice
Each day there is one card: a headline, a short read, sometimes a question worth bringing to dinner. Carry it, or let it go. There is no wrong answer, nothing to catch up on, and no feed waiting underneath.

the house you build by noticing
Every thought you carry adds a room to your house of thought, one room for each field. The ones you let go settle as soil beneath it, because what you pass on shapes you too. A few weeks in, the house tells you something a streak never could: not how often you showed up, but how far your thinking has traveled.

the margin
Now and then, today’s thought turns out to rhyme with one you kept a month ago. A single line appears in the margin, naming what the two share. Psychologists call this elaborative encoding. You will know it as the moment Tuesday’s idea finally made sense on Friday.

ask your own collection
Walking into a hard conversation, a big decision, a pitch? Ask what your collection thinks. The answer draws on the ideas you have carried and quotes them back to you. Not the whole internet. Yours.

your thinker type
Keep a few sample ideas when you begin and you will meet your type, from The Lens Shifter to The Paradox Mind. It decides which ideas find you first.

built to be closed
No endless scroll. No streak to protect. No guilt for a missed day. On iPhone and iPad, on your Lock Screen and your Home Screen, and then out of your way.

free, for good
The daily idea, carry and let go, every thought you have ever kept, your house of thought, your type, your journal, widgets and Siri.

membership
More room to think: up to 10 Ask questions a day instead of one, every margin instead of the first few, the full bed of thoughts you let go, and a written portrait of how your mind works. Monthly or yearly, with 7 days free on yearly, or once for life. Subscriptions renew automatically unless cancelled at least 24 hours before the end of the current period.

quotes.text:
I'm a marketer, not an engineer. This is the first iOS app I've shipped.

The backstory:
I spent three months on research before writing a line of code. Two things had to be true first: the content had to be genuinely different from the wellness space, and the monetization couldn't contradict what the product was trying to do.

On content: I read research on decision fatigue, attentional residue, and the paradox of choice. Most "thought of the day" apps are fortune cookies with better design. I wanted cards that made people sit with something uncomfortable, not cards that made them feel validated. 1,250 cards written and tagged across 12 content buckets before launch.

On monetisation: most wellness apps monetise by maximising session time, which is directly at odds with a mindfulness tool. I landed on charging for what the app actually does. Seven-day trial, then €1.99 a month or €39.99 lifetime. After trial, content progressively blurs rather than hard-bricking.

What it does:
One thought per day. A headline (max 10 words) and a body (max 120 words). You Carry it or Let Go. The app asks you to close it. Under two minutes. Cards are selected server-side by a Resonance Loop algorithm. Days 1 to 14 cycle through all 12 buckets. From day 15, selection weights toward buckets the person resonates with based on carry/let-go signals, with 20% exploration to prevent filter bubbles and 10% heat (cards with high community share rates).
